classification.difficultyReason: The hardest essential demand is combining reciprocal domain exclusions, three branch signs, one-sided limits, transformed turning points and a nonzero horizontal limit in one sketch. These are routine linked applications of the supplied teaching; neither absolute-value transformation requires an unsignposted insight.

answer.worked:
Keep each $x$-coordinate and reciprocate its nonzero $y$-coordinate.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6.25}&=\frac{4}{25}=0.16\\\frac{1}{-1.5}&=-\frac23\end{aligned}$$
The turning points become $(-1.5,0.16)$ and $(0.4,-\tfrac23)$. The zeros of $f(x)$ give vertical asymptotes $x=0$ and $x=1$; exclude both values from the domain. Since $f(x)\to4$, the horizontal asymptote is $y=\tfrac14$.
The reciprocal has the same sign as $f(x)$: positive for $x<0$ and $x>1$, and negative for $0<x<1$.
$$\begin{aligned}\lim_{x\to0^-}\frac1{f(x)}&=+\infty\\\lim_{x\to0^+}\frac1{f(x)}&=-\infty\\\lim_{x\to1^-}\frac1{f(x)}&=-\infty\\\lim_{x\to1^+}\frac1{f(x)}&=+\infty\end{aligned}$$
Reverse increasing and decreasing behaviour on each continuous branch. The left tail approaches $y=\tfrac14$ from below and the right tail approaches it from above. There are no axis intercepts.
